- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above peak or use lagged mean.
- If sentiment turns negative mid-period, model often fails to correct downward; apply downward bias starting from day of sentiment shift.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >+10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00/0.33 values, model tends to underreact; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to compensate for lag.
- For 30-day forecasts, if first 5 days show upward trend, model often overcorrects later; cap forecast slope after day 5 unless sentiment confirms continuation.
